symptom: describe page wrote `DataSource: selection grid1` for a data view listening to a legacy Forms$DataGrid it only emitted as a "NOT re-executable" comment; check -p and exec refused the page: "widget 'dataView1': selection DataSource references 'grid1' but no widget with that name exists on this page" (mendixlabs/mxcli#1415).
cause: outputWidgetMDLV3 renders each widget independently, so the default branch's decision to drop a widget never reached a sibling that referenced it by name. Now describeWidgetBody (page and snippet bodies) records the dropped names, and a widget whose selection source is dropped is commented out with it — transitively, and re-rendered when the dependent precedes its source in document order.
insight: A per-widget describer cannot keep a cross-widget reference honest: any widget it drops can strand a `selection X` elsewhere, before or after it. Check without -p passes such output (the reference needs the page tree), so only check -p / exec shows it. To reproduce without the FSM template, retype a list view in the fixture BSON: "Forms$ListView\x00" and "Forms$DataGrid\x00" are the same length, so a byte replace gives a real unauthorable widget with nothing else moved. A commented data view still loses data on re-exec, by necessity — the fix makes that visible, not lossless.
